name: 1 m lidar scarp detection restricted to gravity corridors
layers: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM (organiser's 1m_DEM_links.csv; public domain) → scarp-likelihood raster; this session's ±1 km basement-step corridor and basin mask as prior.
signature: Metre-scale topographic steps (scarp height 0.5–5 m, slope break, curvature couplet) — the primary evidence the test-set mappers used.
why: The 1:24k–1:250k catalogue missed low scarps in Quaternary fans; 1 m data resolves them; the corridor removes fan-toe/terrace mimics that have no basement step.
diff: Unlike archived H61-G, which used band-19 slope-ridge dots, this tests 3DEP-derived scarp morphology as multi-line ribbons inside an inverted basement-step corridor. The merged main branch also tested H61-MH, a gravity/inversion-feature out-of-fold habitat model; it did not test this 3DEP scarp-ribbon surface. The terrain raster is a public sibling derivative, not raw DEM/lidar tiles.
gain: Highest expected value by expert prior (PROJECTION, not a score); PRE-PLACEMENT UNIQUENESS STOP: 94.6692% of positive scarp-ribbon surface pixels are within 3 px of the prior near-blanket raster, above the literal 70% threshold. HOLDOUT NOT RUN.
cost: High data volume; public sibling-derived 12-band descriptor file already fetched and SHA-256 verified. One candidate surface built; no holdout or submission slot used.
holdout_status: NOT RUN — strict surface gate stop

name: Piedmont belt: basinward of the inverted bedrock–fill contact
layers: Inverted depth = 0 contour (bedrock outcrop boundary) buffered 0–2 km basinward; band 12 detrended elevation curvature; band 19 slope ridges.
signature: Range-front normal faults step basinward through time; young splays and antithetic strands sit 0–2 km in front of the mapped range-front trace as low scarps across fans.
why: The catalogue holds the main range-front trace; piedmont splays are the commonest unmapped class in Basin-and-Range compilations.
diff: H61-MH included a basin indicator and step/corridor features in a learned model, but did not isolate an explicit 0–2 km basinward piedmont belt as its own spatial hypothesis or emit ribbons there.
gain: Moderate. The screen's highest prior-only enrichment (1.7× random for pixels inside the gravity corridor, all depths) sits at the range fronts. PROJECTION.
cost: Low (all inputs cached). One holdout run.

name: Gravity-step × magnetic-edge conjunction (intrabasin faults offsetting magnetic basement or flows)
layers: Corridor from the inversion; band 3 TMI horizontal-gradient maxima; band 6 tilt zero-crossings; band 9 vertical gradient.
signature: A normal fault that offsets magnetised basement or volcanic flows gives a sharp magnetic edge co-located with the gravity step; GeoDAWN line spacing resolves such edges to ~300 m, unlike regional gravity.
why: Concealed under alluvium; surface mapping cannot see them. Co-location rejects intrabasement density contacts that have no magnetic expression (the lane's named mimic).
diff: H61-MH used the 19 supplied bands in a learned habitat model, but did not implement this explicit gravity-step × magnetic-edge conjunction as a test of the intrabasement-contact mimic; H61-C only proposed magnetic fabric as an oracle.
gain: Low–moderate: precision ×1.5 plausible, recall small (few magnetic basins). PROJECTION.

name: Source-depth consistency filter (Euler SI = 0) to reject intrabasement contacts
layers: Band 13 gravity, band 5 horizontal gradient, band 11 vertical gradient → contact-depth estimate; compare with inverted basin depth.
signature: A basement step has source depth ≈ fill thickness; an intrabasement density contrast has source depth ≫ fill thickness.
why: Directly tests the lane's competing explanation; improves the purity of X1-type candidates.
diff: H61-MH included Euler SI=0 source depth as a weak model feature, but did not implement a hard source-depth-versus-inverted-fill-thickness consistency filter; this decision rule remains untested.
gain: Low: raises precision of a candidate family whose recall is already tiny (X1a 0.023). PROJECTION.

name: Scale-persistent paired-flank basement-step ribbons with magnetic corroboration
layers: Supplied isostatic gravity → provisional inverted basement depth and its horizontal gradients at 200/400/800 m; supplied TMI/tilt/vertical-gradient magnetic bands as corroboration only. GP-1012 calibrates the regional depth scale.
signature: A candidate step has paired cross-profile gradient flanks of opposite sign, coherent strike, and a persistent location across scales; a co-located magnetic edge supports but is not required for the ribbon.
why: Buried basin-interior faults can be omitted or fragmented in the mapped catalogue. Pairing, strike continuity, and scale persistence may suppress isolated density contacts/noise while allowing multi-line fault ribbons under alluvium; magnetics provide an independent but imperfect corroborating signature.
diff: Distinct from H61-MH, which used supplied bands and inversion-derived variables in a learned habitat model, and from H61-H, which proposed simple gravity/magnetic edge conjunction. This untested rule matches paired flank geometry and scale persistence before ribbon emission; it uses no catalogue-derived candidate features.
gain: Low-to-moderate expected gain, PROJECTION ONLY: paired-flank geometry may improve precision, while requiring magnetic corroboration can lose faults without magnetised offsets. No measured DTI.
cost: Medium-high: compute multi-scale derivatives, orientation-aware cross-profile pairs, and pre-placement registry gates; run one holdout only if the surface first clears.
